roleTitle: Service Analytics Analyst, Lift and Escalator Maintenance
jobDescription: Our company maintains lifts and escalators in offices, hospitals and shopping centres under monthly service contracts. Field engineers log every callout on handheld devices, and the service analytics team turns those logs into reports for branch managers and key accounts. The analyst will build and look after the callout data model, investigate repeat faults with the technical support engineers, help planners decide where preventive visits go, and publish the monthly contract performance report. Improvements are reported as before-and-after comparisons over defined periods, taken from the callout system's records.
requirements: Builds and maintains a data model of field callouts in SQL.
Investigates repeat faults and shows a measured reduction in repeat callouts against a defined baseline period.
Produces the monthly contract performance report for branch managers and key accounts.
Supports the planning of preventive maintenance visits with fault data.
Publishes dashboards in Power BI or a comparable tool with row-level security by branch.

evidence.text: Designed the callout fact table and the equipment and site dimensions in SQL Server at Ardent Lift Services, loading the handheld callout logs every night.

Analysed repeat callouts on hydraulic lifts and, with the technical support engineers, introduced a door-operator inspection step. Repeat callouts within 30 days on the south branch went from 11.8% of callouts in July to December 2022 to 7.1% in July to December 2023.
Published the monthly contract performance report (response times, first-time fix rate, open faults) for eleven key accounts and the four branch managers.
Each quarter, listed lifts by fault frequency so that the planners could book preventive visits for the most fault-prone units first.
Built the branch dashboards in Power BI and refreshed them after each nightly load.

Work sample: the repeat-callout review pack for the south branch, with callout-system extracts for July to December 2022 (repeat rate 11.8%) and July to December 2023 (repeat rate 7.1%), the definition of a repeat callout (same unit, any fault, within 30 days) and the branch manager's sign-off dated 15 January 2024.

HR verification note: employment at Ardent Lift Services from February 2021 to August 2024 as Service Data Analyst was confirmed by the former employer's HR department in a letter dated 3 September 2024.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate can start on 4 November and would need a pool car for the monthly key-account visits.

propositions.text: After the candidate's repeat-callout analysis and the door-operator inspection step introduced with the technical support engineers, repeat callouts within 30 days on the south branch went from 11.8% (July to December 2022) to 7.1% (July to December 2023), per the signed-off review pack.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the change and both periods, and the work sample carries the extracts, the repeat-callout definition and the branch manager's sign-off.

propositions.text: The candidate published the monthly contract performance report for eleven key accounts and four branch managers.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the report, its contents and audience directly.

propositions.text: The candidate designed the callout fact table and its equipment and site dimensions in SQL Server, loading the callout logs nightly.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the data model work directly.

gold.expectedGap: Power BI dashboards are documented, but whether they used row-level security by branch is not stated.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the repeat-callout result with its definition, both six-month periods, the south-branch scope and the sign-off; do not extend it to other branches or present the inspection step as the candidate's sole work.
followUpTargets: Ask how access to the branch dashboards was controlled and whether row-level security was set up.
